retainedPassages.text: Data Center Corridor Roundup: 3 Updates Local Vendors Should Watch This Week — BorderPlex Source 🏪 Local business? Claim your free listing — get found by regional procurement teams → ✕ Directory Blog Opportunities Guide About Pro List Your Business Español Directory Blog Opportunities Guide About Pro Español ← All articles EN Data Center Corridor Data Center Corridor Roundup: 3 Updates Local Vendors Should Watch This Week ✍️ BorderPlex Source 📅 May 18, 2026 The BorderPlex data center corridor is moving fast, but not every project is at the same stage. In the same regional conversation, local reporting has placed three major campuses on the map: Meta’s data center in Northeast El Paso, Project Jupiter in Santa Teresa, and the proposed Fort Bliss / Carlyle data center on Army land in Far East El Paso.[^1] For local contractors and service providers, the practical takeaway is simple: the opportunity is real, but the timing, procurement paths, and unanswered questions are different for each project. El Paso Matters described the three-project buildout as potentially requiring almost 6.5 gigawatts of electricity demand, while noting that El Paso Electric has about 2.9 gigawatts of generation capacity and has met a highest-ever demand of about 2.3 gigawatts.[^1] That comparison matters because power, water, permitting, and utility design are not side issues. They shape construction timelines, site scopes, public review, and the types of vendors that may be needed first. Proj
